lanes.title: Crate licences for a shipped MIT/Apache product
lanes.verifier_note: Checked all 20 warrant sources by direct retrieval: live WebFetch of every SPDX/cargo-deny/Mozilla page plus a representative sample of docs.rs source pages, cross-checked against the local cargo registry mirror (equivalent per brief) for midly-0.5.3, abc-parser-0.4.0, assert_no_alloc-1.1.2, cpal-0.18.2 and midir-0.11.0 Cargo.toml and LICENSE files at the pinned versions, plus a direct directory listing to confirm cpal 0.18.2 ships no NOTICE file. All 20 source claim sentences held up, several to the word (SPDX BSD-1-Clause text is an exact match to assert_no_alloc's own shipped LICENSE; Apache-2.0 section 4(d) matches cpal's LICENSE verbatim; the cargo-deny gotcha 'GNU licenses are treated pedantically' is a literal quote from the current docs page). This lane has zero checks[] entries across all 10 recipes -- no compile-oracle or config-parse verification anywhere, unlike the Rust-code lanes -- so nothing mechanically catches a bad worked example. That is exactly where the defects clustered: the two recipes that hand-write cargo-deny TOML both got the schema wrong. The exceptions example used a nonexistent `crate = "..."` key where the real PackageSpec key is `name`; the clarify example described `path` and `hash` as flat siblings of `expression` and omitted the required `name` key entirely, where the real schema nests them as `license-files = [{ path, hash }]` alongside a required top-level `name`. Both corrected below with the literal counter-example from the docs. The underlying licensing law itself (Unlicense/MIT/BSD-1-Clause/Apache-2.0/MPL-2.0 obligations) is stated accurately and with real precision throughout, including the non-obvious Apache-2.0-only vs MIT-OR-Apache-2.0 NOTICE-propagation distinction and the BSD-1-Clause source-only (no binary-form clause) nuance; several recipes appropriately self-flag their wasm-vs-native binary-linkage claims as unverified assumptions in gotchas rather than presenting them as settled fact, which is why those are marked directional rather than downgraded.

lanes.title: Native audio and MIDI host
lanes.verifier_note: Checked every claim against the pinned crate source itself (cpal 0.18.2, midir 0.11.0, rtrb 0.4.0, ringbuf 0.5.2, assert_no_alloc 1.1.2), read from the local cargo registry cache at those exact versions (byte-identical to the cited docs.rs source pages), plus Microsoft Learn for WASAPI/WinMM platform semantics (IAudioClient::Initialize error table, MIM_DATA message, DRV_QUERYDEVICEINTERFACE). All 20 warrant sources retrieved and individually accurate; 0 unfindable, 0 outright refuted. 4 of 10 recipes needed a correction. The systemic weakness: every recipe correctly cites 'the code does X', but several then add an uncited platform-semantic gloss on top ('because the default device changed', 'the std feature', 'try_push/try_pop', 'midiInGetDevCapsW supplies the id') that turns out to be imprecise or wrong when checked against Microsoft's own docs or the crate's Cargo.toml feature gates. Checks are honest about being compile-only where behaviour can't be observed without hardware, but one check (assert_no_alloc) omits the #[global_allocator] registration its own recipe's 'how' requires, so it demonstrates less than the prose claims.

recipes.name: Request cpal BufferSize::Fixed on WASAPI shared-mode output
recipes.what: cpal’s WASAPI backend always creates shared-mode streams, and BufferSize::Fixed only requests a callback size that the host may round.
recipes.how: Set StreamConfig.buffer_size to BufferSize::Fixed(frames) before calling build_output_stream. Query SupportedBufferSize::Range on the device to pick a valid value. Expect shared mode; cpal does not expose exclusive mode.
recipes.gotchas: Requesting BufferSize::Fixed does not guarantee that exact size; WASAPI may round. Cpal does not expose exclusive mode; shared mode is always used.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the host audio output path; use BufferSize::Fixed to control latency when playing committed events through the oscillator.
recipes.verify_note: lib.rs BufferSize doc: host may round, no size guaranteed (verbatim). wasapi/device.rs: 'always create voices in shared mode'. No AUDCLNT_SHAREMODE_EXCLUSIVE anywhere in cpal src/. Check's SampleRate/FrameCount are u32 aliases; compiles.

checks.label: cpal BufferSize::Fixed and shared mode compile

sources.title: cpal 0.18.2 src/lib.rs
sources.claim: When BufferSize::Fixed(x) is specified, the host may round to hardware-supported values and no guarantees can be made about the actual callback size.

sources.title: cpal 0.18.2 src/host/wasapi/device.rs
sources.claim: The WASAPI device implementation comments state that cpal always creates voices in shared mode, therefore all samples go through an audio processor to mix them together.

recipes.name: Use OutputCallbackInfo playback timestamp for latency alignment
recipes.what: cpal output callbacks receive an OutputCallbackInfo whose timestamp contains a callback instant and a predicted playback instant derived from the device clock and buffered frames.
recipes.how: In the output callback, read info.timestamp().playback as a StreamInstant. On WASAPI this is computed from IAudioClock::GetPosition, frames_written, and stream_latency. Use playback minus callback to estimate latency.
recipes.gotchas: playback is a prediction, not a hardware interrupt timestamp; subtracting callback from playback gives latency but not sample-accurate device time.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the host sample clock; use the playback instant to align the law's integer sample timeline with the audio device.
recipes.verify_note: timestamp.rs host table lists WASAPI = QueryPerformanceCounter(). wasapi/stream.rs output_timestamp(): playback = callback + buffered + stream_latency; callback comes from clock_position() -> audio_clock.GetPosition.

checks.label: OutputCallbackInfo timestamp fields accessible

sources.title: cpal 0.18.2 src/timestamp.rs
sources.claim: OutputStreamTimestamp contains a callback StreamInstant and a playback StreamInstant, and on WASAPI the time source for StreamInstant is QueryPerformanceCounter().

sources.title: cpal 0.18.2 src/host/wasapi/stream.rs
sources.claim: The output_timestamp function derives playback by adding stream.stream_latency and the duration of buffered frames to the callback instant obtained from IAudioClock::GetPosition.

recipes.name: Handle cpal WASAPI xruns and device changes in error callback
recipes.what: The cpal WASAPI backend forwards discontinuities as ErrorKind::Xrun and device removals as DeviceNotAvailable or StreamInvalidated on the error callback.
recipes.how: Provide an error callback to build_output_stream. Match on err.kind(): ErrorKind::Xrun for glitches, ErrorKind::DeviceNotAvailable when the endpoint is unplugged, and ErrorKind::StreamInvalidated when the default device changes.
recipes.gotchas: ErrorKind::Xrun is only emitted on the input path in cpal 0.18.2; output underruns are not explicitly flagged as Xrun in the WASAPI backend.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on host reliability; route ErrorKind::Xrun and DeviceNotAvailable to the law's error log so replay can remain deterministic.
recipes.verify_note: cpal's error-code mapping is exact, and Xrun-input-only gotcha is confirmed (process_output has zero Xrun logic). But 'StreamInvalidated when the default device changes' is wrong per MS Learn; see corrections.

corrections.claim: 'StreamInvalidated when the default device changes' is wrong. MS Learn: AUDCLNT_E_RESOURCES_INVALIDATED fires when the stream is suspended, an exclusive/offload stream disconnects, a packaged app is quiesced, or a protected-output stream closes -- not on default-device change.

checks.label: cpal error callback handles ErrorKind

sources.title: cpal 0.18.2 src/host/wasapi/stream.rs
sources.claim: In process_input, the WASAPI stream emits ErrorKind::Xrun when the AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_DATA_DISCONTINUITY flag is set.

sources.title: cpal 0.18.2 src/host/wasapi/mod.rs
sources.claim: Windows error codes AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED and AUDCLNT_E_ENDPOINT_CREATE_FAILED map to ErrorKind::DeviceNotAvailable, and AUDCLNT_E_RESOURCES_INVALIDATED maps to ErrorKind::StreamInvalidated.

recipes.name: Send events to audio callback via lock-free rtrb or ringbuf queue
recipes.what: Both rtrb and ringbuf provide single-producer single-consumer queues that are lock-free and allocate only on construction, making them safe for real-time audio callbacks.
recipes.how: Create a RingBuffer::new(capacity) (rtrb) or HeapRb::new(capacity) (ringbuf) on the host thread before starting the stream. Move the Consumer into the cpal callback and the Producer stays on the host thread. Use try_push and try_pop (or pop) so the callback never blocks.
recipes.gotchas: rtrb requires std or alloc by default; ringbuf 0.5 uses edition 2024 and requires the std feature for HeapRb. Neither queue provides blocking pop, so the callback must poll.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the host-to-callback event delivery; adopt a wait-free SPSC queue so the audio callback never blocks or allocates.
recipes.verify_note: Core 'what' fully sourced: rtrb lib.rs says lock-free/wait-free, alloc-once; ringbuf lib.rs literally says 'Lock-free SPSC'; SharedRb uses AtomicUsize+Acquire/Release. Two gotcha-level naming/feature claims need fixing; see corrections.

corrections.claim: 'requires std feature for HeapRb' is imprecise: alias.rs/macros.rs gate HeapRb::new() on feature="alloc" only; std enables alloc by default but alloc alone suffices. Also 'try_push and try_pop (or pop)' overstates rtrb: rtrb only has push()/pop(); try_push/try_pop is ringbuf-only naming.

checks.label: rtrb SPSC queue works across threads without blocking

sources.title: rtrb 0.4.0 src/lib.rs
sources.claim: Reading from and writing into the ring buffer is lock-free and wait-free; a fixed-capacity buffer is allocated on construction and no more memory is allocated afterwards.

sources.title: ringbuf 0.5.2 src/rb/shared.rs
sources.claim: SharedRb synchronizes producer and consumer via AtomicUsize indices with Ordering::Acquire and Ordering::Release, providing a lock-free SPSC implementation.

recipes.name: Wrap oscillator callback in assert_no_alloc with cpal equilibrium buffer
recipes.what: assert_no_alloc aborts or warns if the audio callback allocates, and cpal pre-fills the output buffer with silence before invoking the callback.
recipes.how: Register the global allocator AllocDisabler in main (debug builds). Inside the cpal output callback, wrap all work in assert_no_alloc(|| { ... }). Because cpal calls fill_equilibrium before the callback, any slot the callback does not overwrite remains silent.
recipes.gotchas: assert_no_alloc only catches allocations made through the global allocator; it does not prevent Vec growth inside the closure unless the global allocator is hooked. In release mode with default features it is a no-op.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the real-time guarantee; wrap the oscillator callback in assert_no_alloc to enforce zero allocation on the audio thread.
recipes.verify_note: Both sources exact: README 'abort or print a warning'; wasapi/stream.rs fill_equilibrium() runs before data_callback() (line 886 vs 894). But the check never registers AllocDisabler as #[global_allocator]; see corrections.

corrections.claim: Check omits '#[global_allocator] static A: AllocDisabler', which the recipe's own 'how' and README step 2 require. Without it, assert_no_alloc(||...) compiles/runs but checks nothing -- it only proves the closure nests inside a cpal callback, not that allocation is caught.

checks.label: assert_no_alloc wraps cpal callback pattern compiles
with AllocDisabler as #[global_allocator], an allocation inside assert_no_alloc aborts (debug build); one outside it is allowed

recipes.name: Interpret midir WinMM input timestamps as microseconds since start
recipes.what: midir’s WinMM backend delivers input callback timestamps in microseconds, converted from the Windows MIDI driver’s millisecond timestamp that starts at zero when midiInStart is called.
recipes.how: In the MidiInput::connect callback, treat the first u64 argument as microseconds elapsed since the connection began. Do not assume it is an absolute clock; it is an arbitrary epoch fixed for the lifetime of the MidiInputConnection.
recipes.gotchas: The timestamp epoch is fixed per MidiInputConnection, but it is not comparable across connections or processes. Do not assume it is Unix time.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on MIDI input ingestion; treat the u64 microseconds as relative to midiInStart and convert to the law's integer sample timeline.
recipes.verify_note: handler.rs: 'timestamp = timestamp as u64 * 1000' verbatim. MS Learn MIM_DATA page independently confirms dwTimestamp is ms 'beginning at zero when the midiInStart function was called'; connect() calls midiInStart once (mod.rs:329).

checks.label: midir input callback signature and timestamp type compile

sources.title: midir 0.11.0 README.md
sources.claim: midir supports the WinMM backend on Windows.

sources.title: midir 0.11.0 src/backend/winmm/handler.rs
sources.claim: The WinMM input handler sets data.message.timestamp = timestamp as u64 * 1000, converting the dwTimestamp (milliseconds since midiInStart) to microseconds.

recipes.name: Anchor midir microseconds to cpal StreamInstant and re-anchor for drift
recipes.what: Because midir timestamps and cpal StreamInstant come from independent clocks, the host must establish an anchor and re-anchor periodically to keep the law’s sample clock aligned.
recipes.how: At stream start (or first MIDI event), record both the midir microseconds value and cpal’s StreamInstant (or frames_written). For each subsequent MIDI event, compute delta_us = midi_timestamp - anchor_midi, then convert to samples with delta_us * sample_rate / 1_000_000. Re-sample both clocks every few seconds to correct drift.
recipes.gotchas: Integer division when converting microseconds to samples truncates; accumulate remainders to avoid systematic timing drift. Re-anchor at least every few seconds.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the integer sample clock; re-anchor the midir-to-cpal offset regularly because the two device clocks drift independently.
recipes.verify_note: handler.rs confirms the ms*1000 conversion; timestamp.rs table confirms WASAPI/QueryPerformanceCounter(). Check's delta_us/sample arithmetic matches 'how' exactly and type-checks (StreamInstant::ZERO exists).

checks.label: midir timestamp and cpal StreamInstant types can be combined

recipes.name: Enumerate midir WinMM input ports by interface ID
recipes.what: MidiInput::ports returns a vector of MidiInputPort values on Windows via the WinMM midiInGetNumDevs and midiInGetDevCapsW APIs.
recipes.how: Create a MidiInput, call ports(), then iterate and call port_name() for display and id() for a stable string identifier. Use the id string to reconnect to the same physical device across restarts.
recipes.gotchas: WinMM port indices can change when devices are plugged or unplugged; use port.id() (the interface ID string) for stable identification, not the port index.

lanes.title: Integer musical time: ticks, tempo maps, samples
lanes.verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes by re-deriving every formula and running 18 counter-examples through the pinned rustc 1.98.1 oracle (host + wasm32-unknown-unknown/cdylib), including two checks the lane itself lacked: an overflow-checks on/off/default probe at opt-level 3, and a direct FFI probe of a u128 extern "C" signature. Every given check's stdout reproduced exactly, and every SMF/Rust fact traced to midly 0.5.3 (event.rs, primitive.rs) or current doc.rust-lang.org pages held up; nothing was refuted. Systemic weakness: citation precision inside midly and reflexive padding. The two u128-tempo-map recipes cite src/primitive.rs for 'tempo=u24, delta=u28', but that tie is only made in src/event.rs (MetaMessage::Tempo(u24), TrackEvent.delta: u28) -- primitive.rs defines just the generic bit-width wrapper types, forcing me to retrieve the other file to actually confirm the claim. Separately, the generic u128-primitive-type doc page is cited as a stock second source on 5 of 10 recipes regardless of relevance (e.g. the f64-precision and remainder-carry recipes never touch u128), while the one recipe that actually needed an ABI citation (u128 across the wasm extern "C" boundary) cited two sources that never mention FFI/ABI at all and missed doc.rust-lang.org's own i128 'ABI compatibility' note -- which is exactly the passage that explains why wasm32-unknown-unknown (no C/C++ toolchain) leaves u128 there unstable, confirmed live when my counter-example compiled silently into a 3-argument wasm export instead of a clean 1-in/1-out signature.

recipes.name: Compute tick-to-microseconds with u128 intermediate and floor
recipes.what: SMF stores tempo as u24 microseconds-per-quarter and tick deltas as u28; the law evaluates the exact rational tick×tempo÷PPQ in u128 and floors once per segment.
recipes.how: Inside an extern "C" function, write `let us = ((tick as u128 * tempo as u128) / ppq as u128) as u64;`. The single integer division is the floor.
recipes.gotchas: Dividing before multiplying truncates early and loses tempo resolution; u64 intermediates overflow at max tick × max tempo.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the likely second integer timeline in samples: the wasm cdylib must convert ticks to exact microseconds without floating point.
recipes.verify_note: Host port of the wasm check ran: stdout 500000, exact. Wasm build with #[unsafe(no_mangle)] compiles on 1.98.1/ed2024. Gotcha confirmed: u64.checked_mul at max tick x u24::MAX tempo overflows; the u128 product does not.

corrections.claim: Source cites src/primitive.rs for 'tempo=u24, delta=u28'; that tie is made in src/event.rs (MetaMessage::Tempo(u24); TrackEvent.delta: u28). primitive.rs only defines the generic bit-width wrapper types, not their use.

recipes.name: Compute tick-to-samples through tempo map with u128
recipes.what: Samples are derived from ticks by the exact rational tick×tempo×sample_rate÷(PPQ×1_000_000), computed in u128 and floored once.
recipes.how: Compute `let num = tick as u128 * tempo as u128 * sample_rate as u128; let den = ppq as u128 * 1_000_000u128; let samples = (num / den) as u64;` inside the exported function.
recipes.gotchas: Reordering to divide early introduces rounding errors; the full numerator must stay in u128 until the final division.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the likely separately pinned renderer: sample positions must be exact integers computed from the tempo map inside the wasm law.

recipes.name: Calculate bar and beat from tick under SMF time signatures
recipes.what: SMF FF 58 stores numerator and a power-of-two denominator; bar/beat arithmetic uses ticks_per_beat = PPQ × 4 ÷ 2^denom and ticks_per_bar = ticks_per_beat × num.
recipes.how: Parse the four TimeSignature bytes; compute `beat_unit = 1u32 << denom_exp; ticks_per_beat = (ppq * 4) / beat_unit;` then derive bar, beat and tick-in-beat with `/` and `%`.
recipes.gotchas: The denominator byte is the exponent, not the written denominator; e.g., 4/4 uses denom_exp = 2.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the integer tick timeline: the law must locate events in bars and beats for display and looping without floating point.
recipes.verify_note: Ran the check verbatim (stdout '1 0 0') plus my own non-boundary case tick=2500: got '1 1 100', matching hand derivation. SMF spec (retrieved separately) confirms the denominator byte is the power-of-2 exponent.

recipes.name: Refuse on overflow with checked arithmetic
recipes.what: The law uses checked_mul and checked_add so that any overflow in time calculations returns a refusal instead of wrapping or panicking.
recipes.how: Chain `tick.checked_mul(tempo)?.checked_add(carry)?` and propagate None as a refusal event to the host.
recipes.gotchas: Unchecked `*` panics in debug and wraps in release by default; strict_mul always panics, which is unsuitable for a law that must refuse gracefully.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on deterministic replay: an overflow must produce a defined refusal in the action log, not a wrap or trap.

recipes.name: Carry division remainders across tempo segments
recipes.what: Floor division is not associative across segment sums: floor(a/c)+floor(b/c) can be less than floor((a+b)/c); the law carries remainders to keep cumulative time exact.
recipes.how: For each segment compute `quot = tick * tempo / PPQ` and `rem = (tick * tempo) % PPQ`; add `rem` to the next segment’s numerator before division.
recipes.gotchas: Flooring each segment independently drops fractional ticks that accumulate into audible micro-timing drift across tempo changes.
recipes.engine_note: Bears on the integer tempo map: crossing a tempo boundary must not lose fractional ticks between the score and the sample timeline.
recipes.verify_note: Ran the check verbatim: stdout '3 2' then '3' -- confirms floor((a+b)/c) != a/c+b/c, and the remainder-carry sum recovers the exact total. Both cited sources are true but unused; the check only uses plain u64 %,/.

lanes.title: Score ingest inside a wasm law: SMF, MusicXML, ABC
lanes.verifier_note: Checked all 7 recipes by reading the docs.rs source mirror at pinned versions from the local cargo registry (midly-0.5.3, musicxml-1.1.2, quick-xml-0.42.0, roxmltree-0.21.1, abc-parser-0.4.0), cross-checked against oracle-jam/Cargo.toml (the actual wiring checks[] compile against), plus two compile_oracle.py counter-examples. All 14 cited source claims held up individually. Three recipes needed correction: recipe 3's engine_note wrongly treats 'Err-as-fatal' as equivalent to enabling midly's strict feature (Malformed is never raised without it); recipe 4 falsely calls quick-xml 0.42 'a no_std pull parser' (no such feature exists in its Cargo.toml or source); recipe 7's engine_note prescribes arithmetic on abc-parser's Length type that does not compile (no Mul impl, private field — confirmed E0369 and E0616 by counter-example). Systemic weakness: oracle-jam/Cargo.toml pins midly alone to match its recipe's recommended feature set (default-features=false, alloc); musicxml/quick-xml/roxmltree/abc-parser are all built with plain defaults, so any recipe recommending a non-default configuration for those four crates (recipe 4's musicxml default-features=false) can never be exercised end-to-end by this lane's own compile oracle -- only the crate's default happy path is ever mechanically checked, and that is exactly where the false and uncompilable claims clustered.

recipes.name: Configure midly for wasm32-unknown-unknown
recipes.what: Using midly with `default-features = false, features = ["alloc"]` enables `Smf::parse` while avoiding `std` and `rayon` (parallel) dependencies.
recipes.how: In `Cargo.toml`, specify `midly = { version = "0.5.3", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }`. This provides the `Smf` type and allocation-backed parsing without requiring OS threads or the standard library.
recipes.gotchas: If `alloc` is omitted, `Smf::parse` is unavailable, and you must use the lower-level `parse` function which returns iterators.
recipes.engine_note: Crucial for the wasm law, which has no threads (rayon would fail to compile or run) and operates in a `no_std` or restricted `std` environment.
recipes.verify_note: midly-0.5.3 Cargo.toml: default=[alloc,std,parallel]; parallel needs rayon. lib.rs: Smf unavailable w/o alloc. oracle-jam pins midly exactly as recipe recommends (default-features=false, features=[alloc]).

recipes.name: Map MusicXML divisions to fixed PPQ
recipes.what: MusicXML's `<divisions>` element specifies ticks per quarter note. This must be mapped to the law's fixed PPQ using integer arithmetic.
recipes.how: Calculate `(note_duration * fixed_ppq) / divisions`. If `(note_duration * fixed_ppq) % divisions != 0`, the note's exact timing cannot be represented in the law's fixed PPQ and must be refused.
recipes.gotchas: Divisions can change mid-score in MusicXML. The mapping must use the currently active `<divisions>` value.
recipes.engine_note: The law strictly uses one fixed PPQ. Any MusicXML file with tuplets or durations that do not align with this PPQ must be rejected to maintain deterministic integer state.

recipes.name: Process MusicXML backup and forward elements
recipes.what: MusicXML uses `<backup>` and `<forward>` elements to move the time cursor backward and forward, coordinating multiple voices.
recipes.how: Maintain a running integer time cursor for the current measure. When encountering a `Forward` element, add its `duration.content.0` to the cursor. For a `Backup` element, subtract its duration.
recipes.gotchas: Backup and forward durations are in the current `<divisions>` units, so they must be converted to the law's fixed PPQ before adjusting the global integer timeline.
recipes.engine_note: The law flattens all voices into a single integer timeline of onsets. Backup/forward are essential for resolving polyphony into this flat timeline.

recipes.name: Parse ABC notation with abc-parser
recipes.what: The `abc-parser` 0.4.0 crate parses ABC text into a `TuneBook` AST using PEG, supporting notes, tuplets, and repeats, but lacks chord symbols and macros.
recipes.how: Call `abc_parser::abc::tune_book(text)` to get a `TuneBook`. Iterate over `tunes`, then `body.lines`, matching on `TuneLine::Music` to extract `MusicSymbol::Note`.
recipes.gotchas: ABC lengths are expressed as `f32` (e.g., `Length(0.5)`). These floats must be converted to exact integer ticks at the fixed PPQ, rejecting any that lose precision.
recipes.engine_note: Because ABC lengths are floats in this crate, the law must strictly verify that `(length * base_ticks).round() == (length * base_ticks)` to prevent floating-point non-determinism from leaking into the state.
recipes.verify_note: README/datatypes confirm parsing + Length(f32). engine_note's '(length*base_ticks).round()==...' is impossible: Length has no Mul impl (E0369) and a private field (E0616) -- confirmed via compile-oracle counter-example.
